messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: customer AsterionHealth (private VPC) — increased 502/Upstream errors observed from Dedicated pool 'dedicated-prod-42' starting ~2026-03-17T09:12:05Z. NLB target health flapping reported. Auto-escalate to #incidents.
emma_oncall: On it. I’m taking pager for this incident. Opening handoff. :ambulance:
alice_sre: ACK. ETA 2m. Any immediate customer impact metrics?
carla_support: Asterion CS reports ~40% of requests failing with 502s to the inference endpoint since 09:12 UTC. They attached sample request/response logs. Link: https://redwood.corp/attachments/asterion/502-samples
karen_asterion: We're seeing model responses time out or 502s during inference calls — causing dropped requests in their UI. Impacting a small set of enterprise users on dedicated pool.
bob_neteng: I see NLB metrics spike on target 10.12.5.21/22 — health checks toggling UNHEALTHY -> HEALTHY rapidly. Suspect either healthcheck path/port mismatch or security group blocking health probes.
alice_sre: Can someone run target-health and NLB health logs please? I want target status and any 502 origin traces.
bob_neteng: running:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-dedicated-prod-42/abcdef123
```
Output (trimmed):
```
"TargetHealthDescriptions": [
  {"Target": {"Id": "10.12.5.21", "Port": 8080}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Health checks failed"}},
  {"Target": {"Id": "10.12.5.22", "Port": 8080}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Target timed out"}}
]
```
bob_neteng: NLB configured for TCP health check on port 8080 but app is answering HTTP/1.1 health path /healthz returning 200. However, I see a recent SG change at 09:11 UTC that removed the load-balancer health check IP range from NACL/SG. Looking into audit.
emma_oncall: @bob_neteng mark it as high priority — if SG blocks probes, targets get drained causing 502s.
dan_prodeng: From runtime side: nodes logged repeated connection resets and kv-cache misses at 09:12. We also had a rolling infra deploy 09:05-09:10 for node agent update in dedicated-prod-42; might be correlated.
alice_sre: Two-pronged: (1) get healthchecks back — apply SG rule to allow ELB healthcheck range OR re-add previous rule rollback; (2) if traffic still failing, shift traffic to fallback pool/failover region.
bob_neteng: I can reapply the SG rule. Rolling back the 09:11 SG change now. Command:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 192.0.2.0/28
```
carla_support: FYI I asked Asterion for any changes on their side — they deny any config change.
bob_neteng: SG rollback applied. Waiting for target to pass health checks. Observing CloudWatch...
(2m later)
bob_neteng: Targets moving to healthy: 10.12.5.21 -> healthy, 10.12.5.22 -> healthy. NLB traffic stable. Upstream 502 count trending down.
emma_oncall: Can telemetry confirm request success rate returning to baseline?
alice_sre: Checking traces — 502s reduced to <2% over last 5m from 40%. Logs show healthchecks were indeed failing with RST from targets due to SG.
dan_prodeng: Confirmed runtime kv-cache warmed back, no ongoing restarts. The rolling deploy likely made nodes briefly sensitive but SG change is the root cause of ongoing fail-open.
karen_asterion: Thanks — seeing service improving on our side. Any ETA to fully close?
alice_sre: Remaining action items: (A) run a 30m observation window, (B) remediation postmortem — investigate why SG change landed during maintenance window; (C) add guardrail preventing removal of LB health CIDR from customer-dedicated SGs.
emma_oncall: I’ll keep the incident open for 30m and then hand back to ops. Notifying customer success for update to Asterion.
carla_support: Sent customer update summarizing cause and mitigation. They asked for root cause report once available.
bob_neteng: Follow-ups: pin down who applied SG change (audit shows operator id svc-deploy), adding automated alert when target health flips >5% in 60s.
dan_prodeng: We'll also add a healthcheck compatibility test to our deploy job to avoid port/path mismatches during agent updates.
alice_sre: Good. Closing timeline: incident start 2026-03-17T09:12:05Z, mitigation rollback at 09:15:30Z, baseline recovered by 09:20Z. Postmortem assigned: #PM-1892, owner @dan_prodeng.
emma_oncall: Incident resolved for paging. Leaving channel at 09:45 UTC after observation window. :white_check_mark:
carla_support: Customer notified and happy with the quick mitigation. Marking as resolved from CS side.
incident-bot: Incident closed in PagerDuty (PD-4721) by emma_oncall. Tags: vpc, nlb, security-group, dedicated-pool, customer-impact
